questions.q: The number of species below that have two lone pairs of electrons in their central atom is ___ (Round off to the Nearest integer) ${SF}_{4}, {BF}_{4}^{-}, {ClF}_{3}, {AsF}_{3}, {PCl}_{5}, {BrF}_{5}, {XeF}_{4}, {SF}_{6}$
questions.solution:
Two l.p. on central atom is $= {ClF}_{3}, {XeF}_{4}$

The valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) theory is a model used to predict 3-D molecular geometry based on the number of valence shell electron bond pairs among the atoms in a molecule or ion. This model assumes that electron pairs will arrange themselves to minimize repulsion effects from one another.

Consider, ${PF}_{5}, {BrF}_{5}, {PCl}_{3}, {SF}_{6}, {\left[{ICl}_{4}\right]}^{-}, {ClF}_{3}$ and ${IF}_{5}$

Amongst the above molecule(s) ion(s), the number of molecule(s)/ion(s) having ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$ hybridisation is
questions.solution:
Number of hybrid orbitals = Number of bond pair + number of lone pair on central atom.

To have ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$ hybridisation there should be total of 6 (bond pairs + lone pairs). The structure in such case will be octahedral or its derivative structures.

questions.q:
Amongst the following the number of oxide(s) which are paramagnetic in nature is

${Na}_{2}O, {KO}_{2}, {NO}_{2}, {N}_{2}O, {ClO}_{2}, NO, {SO}_{2}, {Cl}_{2}O$
questions.solution:
The magnetic properties of a substance can be determined by examining its electron configuration: If it has unpaired electrons, then the substance is paramagnetic and if all electrons are paired, the substance is then diamagnetic.

${KO}_{2}$ is potassium superoxide. There is one unpaired electron in anti-bonding molecular orbital of superoxide. Potassium superoxide is paramagnetic due to the presence of unpaired electron.

${NO}_{2}, {ClO}_{2}, NO$ are odd electron species. Hence, they are paramagnetic.

The other are monoxide and dioxide contain paired electrons, so they will show diamagnetic behaviour.

questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment value of ${M}^{3 +}$ ion (in gaseous state) from the pairs ${Cr}^{3 +} / {Cr}^{2 +}, {Mn}^{3 +} / {Mn}^{2}, {Fe}^{3 +} / {Fe}^{2 +}$ and ${Co}^{3 +} / {Co}^{2 +}$ that has negative standard electrode potential, is_____ $B . M .$
questions.solution:
Negative value of electrode potential for $\dfrac{{M}^{3 +}}{{M}^{2 +}}$ is for $\dfrac{{Cr}^{+ 3}}{{Cr}^{+ 2}}$

${E}_{\dfrac{{Cr}^{+ 3}}{{Cr}^{+ 2}}}^{0} = - 0 . 41V$

${Cr}^{+ 2}$ acts as a reducing agent readily

Electronic configuration of ${Cr}^{+ 3}ion$ is

$\left[Ar\right]4{s}^{0}3{d}^{3}$

Number of unpaired electrons,$n =$3

Magnetic moment,

$\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}B . M = \sqrt{3\left(3 + 2\right)}B . M$

$= \sqrt{15}B . M ≃ 4B . M$

questions.q:
If ${\left[Cu{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{4}\right]}^{2 +}$ absorbs a light of wavelength $600nm$ for $d - d$ transition, then the value of octahedral crystal field splitting energy for ${\left[Cu{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +}$ will be____$\times {10}^{- 21}J$ [Nearest integer]

(Given : $h = 6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34}Js$ and $c = 3 . 08 \times {10}^{8}{ms}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
${\Delta}_{t} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \left(\dfrac{6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 . 08 \times {10}^{8}}{600 \times {10}^{- 9}}\right) = 340 . 34 \times {10}^{- 21}J$

${\Delta}_{∘} = \dfrac{9}{4}{\Delta}_{t} = \dfrac{9}{4} \times 340 . 34 \times {10}^{- 21} = 765 . 765 \times {10}^{- 21} \approx 766 \times {10}^{21}J$

Note: According to official answer key provided by NTA answer is 745. But according to calculations answer is = 766.

questions.q:
In the ground state of atomic $Fe ( Z = 26 )$, the spin-only magnetic moment is $\times {10}^{- 1}BM$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
[ Given $: \sqrt{3} = 1 . 73, \sqrt{2} = 1 . 41 ]$
questions.solution:
$Fe \to [ Ar ] 4{s}^{2}3{d}^{6}$

Number of unpaired ${e}^{-} = 4$

$\mu = \sqrt{4 ( 4 + 2 )}B . M .$

$\mu = \sqrt{24}B . M$

$\mu = 4 . 89B . M$

$\mu = 48 . 9 \times {10}^{- 1}B . M$

Nearest integer value will be $49 .$

questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the compound with strongest oxidizing ability among ${MnF}_{4}, {MnF}_{3}$ and ${MnF}_{2}$ is_____ $B . M$ (nearest integer)
questions.solution:
The change from Mn3+ to Mn2+ results in the half-filled (d5 ) configuration which has extra stability.So, MnF3 has most oxidising tendency.

Hence, ${MnF}_{3}$ has the strongest oxidizing ability as it undergoes reduction readily.

Spin only magnetic moment is calculated using the following formula

$\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}B . M$

$\mu = \sqrt{4\left(4 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{24} = 4 . 89 = 5B . M$

questions.q:
Consider the following metal complexes :

${\left[Co\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]}^{3 +}$

${\left[CoCl{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{5}\right]}^{2 +}$

${\left[Co ( CN{)}_{6}\right]}^{3 -}$

${\left[Co{\left({NH}_{3}\right)}_{5}\left({H}_{2}O\right)\right]}^{3 +}$

The spin-only magnetic moment value of the complex that absorbs light with shortest wavelength is B.M. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
The complex that absorbs minimum wave length of light has maximum splitting

${\Delta}_{0} ∝ \dfrac{1}{\lambda}{\Delta}_{0} = Crystalfieldstabilizationenergy$

Here, ${CN}^{-}$ being $strongfieldligand$ ,It will have cause CFSE So,${\left[Co ( CN{)}_{6}\right]}^{3 -}$ will absorb minimum wavelength.

The hybridization of Co in ${\left[Co ( CN{)}_{6}\right]}^{3 -}$ will be ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$

As, the complex has no unpaired electrons, spin only magnetic moment will be zero and it is diamagnetic in nature.

questions.q: The oxidation state of manganese in the product obtained in a reaction of potassium permanganate and hydrogen peroxide in basic medium is
questions.solution:
This ${KMnO}_{4}$ is a powerful oxidizing agent in neutral, acidic, and alkaline medium. The ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$ is also an oxidizing agent but in the reaction of ${KMnO}_{4}$ with the ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$. The ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$loses its electron and acts as a reducing agent. In an acidic medium, the${MnO}_{4}^{-}$ ions involve the addition of 5 electrons and the two peroxide ions give out two electrons. In dilute alkaline medium or in neutral medium ${MnO}_{4}^{-}$ ions involve the addition of 3 electrons. The reaction in basic medium is given below.

$2{KMnO}_{4} + 3{H}_{2}{O}_{2}\overset{basicmedium}{⟶}\overset{+ 4}{2{MnO}_{2}} + 3{O}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O + 2KOH$

The oxidation state of $Mn\text{in}{MnO}_{2}$ is $+ 4 .$

questions.q: Acidified potassium permanganate solution oxidises oxalic acid. The spin-only magnetic moment of the mangenese product formed from the above reaction is B.M.___(Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
$2{KMnO}_{4} + 5{H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} + 3{H}_{2}{SO}_{4} \to {K}_{2}{SO}_{4} + 2{MnSO}_{4} + 10{CO}_{2} + 8{H}_{2}O$

In acidic medium, ${Mn}^{7 +}$ gets reduced to ${Mn}^{2 +}$

Mn (II) $= \left[Ar\right]3{d}^{5}$

Number of unpaired electron in ${Mn}^{2 +} = 5$

$\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}B . M$

$\mu = \sqrt{5\left(5 + 2\right)}B . M$

$\mu = 5 . 9B . M$

questions.q: An acidified manganate solution undergoes disproportionation reaction. The spin-only magnetic moment value of the product having manganese in higher oxidation state is____B.M. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$3{MnO}_{4}^{2 -} + 4{H}^{+} ⟶ 2{MnO}_{4}^{-} + {MnO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

As we can see in this reaction oxidised product of reaction is ${MnO}_{4}^{-}$ which has no unpaired electrons. So, magnetic moment will be zero.

$Mn =$ no. of unpaired electrons is '$0$'

$\mu = 0B . M$
